subject: Driftsail: request for latency guardrail & pricing remedy - exec approval needed
messages:
From: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@driftsail.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot ask: latency guardrail and pricing remedy

Hi Mateo / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Driftsail is excited to move into an initial paid pilot. Before we finalize the SOW we have two asks that are blocking procurement on our side:

1) Latency guardrail: for our customer-facing inference calls we need a documented latency SLO of 150ms p50 during the pilot window (60k requests/day). We understand this is tighter than Redwood’s published profile for the model we're planning to use; we are requesting a temporary, documented guardrail/exception for the pilot period.

2) Pricing remedy: because the SLO is tighter than standard, procurement asks for a capped remedy if latency breaches occur during the pilot. Proposal: up to 6% one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice), or alternatively a service-credit ladder tied to % of requests exceeding 200ms.

Attaching our SOW draft and a small sample of latency traces from our staging traffic to illustrate tail behavior. Can Redwood escalate to deal desk / execs for approval of a narrow, time-boxed SLO exception and confirm the remedy approach? We prefer an explicit numeric formula in the SOW rather than vague "reasonable" language.

Sophie
Sophie Lang
Head of Platform
Driftsail AI

Attachments: Driftsail_SOW_v3.pdf, driftsail-latency-samples.csv

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@driftsail.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: latency guardrail and pricing remedy

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the SOW and traces.

Quick confirmation: Redwood can support escalating this to Deal Desk + Execs. A few clarifying questions that will help speed approval:
- Is the 150ms p50 requirement a hard requirement for all endpoints or only for the top-tier customer flows?
- Do you expect steady 60k req/day, or bursty usage with short peaks above that?

Tentative plan from our side: I’ll open a Deal Desk ticket and include Marissa and Jonas for pricing and remediation input. If we can agree on a time-boxed exception (90 days) and a clear, capped remedy formula, we can take to execs for signoff.

I’ll follow up with a summary and recommended language to include in section 6 (SLA & Remedies) of the SOW.

—Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@driftsail.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: latency guardrail and pricing remedy

Sophie, Mateo — I spoke with Deal Desk and Finance. We want to propose a pragmatic compromise to get the pilot underway while limiting systemic risk:

Proposal (commercial + remedy):
- Time-boxed latency carveout: 90 days from pilot start, where Driftsail receives an "operational guardrail" target of p50 <= 150ms for the specified customer-facing endpoints in section A of the SOW. This is an exception to standard model profiles and will be explicitly listed.
- Remedy: a capped service-credit ladder: if >1% of requests exceed 200ms in a billing cycle, Redwood issues service credits equal to 2% of that invoice; if >5% exceed 200ms, credit equals 6% of that invoice. Maximum cumulative credit across the 90-day exception period: 8% of total pilot charges.
- Commercial concession: one-time onboarding credit of 6% applied to first invoice to offset the performance ramp and integration work.

We still need Exec approval for both (a) the temporary deviation from our standard performance guarantees and (b) the maximum credit cap of 8% across the exception window.

Links: HubSpot HS-32451 (deal notes) and provisional DocuSign envelope included for SOW signature once terms are agreed.

If this sounds acceptable to Driftsail, Mateo — can you get an explicit yes from procurement on the cap? Sophie, please confirm that the endpoints in Section A are the only flows you want included.

Best,
Marissa Cole
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@driftsail.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot ask: latency guardrail and pricing remedy

Quick finance ops read — I support the approach with a small modification to the remedy formula to reduce open exposure:

- Keep the time-boxed exception and the onboarding credit.
- Modify ladder: 2% credit if >1% requests exceed 200ms; 5% if >5% exceed 200ms; maximum cumulative credit 6% across 90 days.

Rationale: the original 8% cap plus a 6% onboarding credit pushes our max potential concession to 14% which is high for a short pilot. If Driftsail needs stronger economic protection, consider offering premium support hours (10 hours/month of dedicated SRE support) and an SLA playbook for mitigation instead of higher credit caps.

If Marissa is comfortable with 6% cumulative (with 6% onboarding still applied), we can present to the Execs as lower-risk. If not, we should prepare both variants for approval: (A) commercial variant with 8% cap / 6% onboarding; (B) conservative variant with 6% cap / 6% onboarding + premium SRE support.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Contracts Team <contracts@driftsail.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Pilot ask: latency guardrail and pricing remedy (SOW redlines)

Mateo / Marissa,

Attaching redlines to section 6 of the SOW. Procurement at Driftsail needs the remedy wording to be explicit. Suggested language:

"If live request latency for the endpoints listed in Section A exceeds 200ms for more than X% of requests in a single billing cycle, Redwood will apply a service credit according to the schedule in Appendix B. Service credits will be the sole and exclusive remedy for all latency-related failures during the pilot period."

We also request a clear measurement methodology and a mutual test harness tie-breaker (Redwood and Driftsail will agree on a 24-hour diagnostic window before crediting).

Please review the attached redlines in the SOW and the measurement appendix and advise if Redwood can accept the proposed text or whether you will require Exec-level deviation.

Thanks,
Driftsail Procurement

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sophie Lang <sophie.lang@driftsail.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Exec approval request: Driftsail pilot latency exception and remedy (decision required)

Team — summary for Exec signoff (requested by Procurement):

Background:
- Account: Driftsail AI (pilot, 90-day window).
- Ask: Temporary latency guardrail (p50 <= 150ms for listed endpoints) and explicit service-credit remedy ladder if tail latency exceeds thresholds during billing cycles.
- Attachments: Driftsail_SOW_v3.pdf (with procurement redlines) and driftsail-latency-samples.csv.

Options for Execs (decision required):
A) Conservative (recommended by Finance/Ops: Jonas):
   - Onboarding credit: 6% applied to first invoice.
   - Remedy ladder: 2% credit if >1% requests exceed 200ms; 5% credit if >5% exceed 200ms.
   - Max cumulative credit: 6% across the 90-day exception.
   - Add-on: 10 hours/month dedicated SRE support for pilot period (no charge).

B) Accelerated (commercial-first):
   - Onboarding credit: 6% applied to first invoice.
   - Remedy ladder: 2% credit if >1% exceed 200ms; 6% credit if >5% exceed 200ms.
   - Max cumulative credit: 8% across the 90-day exception.

Risks and mitigation:
- Exposure: Option B maximum concession (14% including onboarding) is material for a short pilot; Option A limits cash exposure and pairs credits with SRE support to improve outcomes.
- Measurement: Driftsail requests explicit measurement language and a 24-hour diagnostic window before crediting. We should accept the measurement appendix language; it protects both parties and reduces disputes.

Request: Exec decision on Option A or Option B and authorization to accept the Procurement redlines in the SOW with the chosen remedy language. If approved, I will execute the Deal Desk package and send final DocuSign for countersignature.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
